Data source overview:
The paper proposes an apprenticeship-learning algorithm that learns from expert demonstrations by fitting a reward function through inverse-reinforcement learning (IRL) while minimising a supervised loss to the expert policy.  Key novelties are the use of sub-differentials to cope with the non-smooth mapping from reward parameters to policies and the use of natural gradients to remove parameter-redundancy problems.  Experiments in grid-worlds and a sailing domain show better accuracy and robustness to feature-scaling errors than a prior max-margin IRL method.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[83]

Inference-strategy justification:
The paper focuses on learning-algorithm design rather than explicit “safety” language.  Moderate inference (confidence 2) was used to frame the algorithmic shortcomings it addresses (e.g. unsafe generalisation, scaling sensitivity) as risks relevant to AI safety and to infer an intervention that recommends systematic robustness testing before deployment.

Extraction-completeness explanation:
All causal-interventional chains explicitly argued in the text—from the stated shortcomings of prior IRL work, through the theoretical tools (natural gradients, Boltzmann smoothing), to empirical findings and resulting algorithmic prescriptions—are captured.  Two interconnected risk pathways converge on three actionable interventions, forming a single connected fabric with no dangling nodes.

Key limitations:
1. The paper contains only small-scale synthetic validation, so edges from validation evidence to interventions are medium confidence (3).  
2. Some node names (e.g. “robustness testing”) rely on moderate inference because the paper implies but does not prescribe them.  
3. Details on deployment-phase safeguards are absent; therefore the fabric covers only model-development and pre-deployment testing phases.
